subject: Capacity handover & cutover sequencing — Clearline Health
messages:
From: Anna Lopez <anna@clearlinehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@clearlinehealth.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Capacity handover & cutover sequencing — Clearline Health

Hi team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we move from Hosted to a Dedicated pool for production traffic, our procurement and SRE leads need a clear handover plan that ties committed capacity to the cutover timeline. High level:

- Target go-live: first week of Jan (internal target)
- Expected steady-state: 120 rps average, 350 rps peak (95th) across two regions (primary US-EAST, DR US-WEST)
- Top concern: predictable latency under 100ms p50 and <250ms p95 post-cutover

Please confirm: what validation steps you need from our side (synthetic traffic, tokenization samples, prompt mix) and what rollback/fallback options you’ll keep ready. Procurement also needs an acceptance milestone we can sign off on post-cutover.

Anna Lopez
Head of AI Ops
Clearline Health

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Anna Lopez <anna@clearlinehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity handover & cutover sequencing — Clearline Health

Anna —

Thanks for the clear targets. Proposed approach (high level):

1) Sizing validation (week 1–2):
   - Redwood runs a preflight using your sample prompt set and token stats; we’ll mirror traffic to a staging Dedicated pool sized to ~1.2x expected steady-state (150 rps) to validate latency under realistic concurrency.
   - We’ll need a 48-hour traffic sample and a representative prompt corpus (ideally 5000 requests covering short/long prompts).

2) Acceptance criteria & sign-offs (week 3):
   - p50 < 90ms, p95 < 240ms, error rate < 0.5% under the mirrored load for a 2-hour smoke window.
   - Once criteria met, Redwood will generate a commit matrix and a one-page acceptance checklist for procurement.

3) Cutover window (week 4):
   - Planned 4-hour blackout window for the final DNS flip + traffic ramp; 1-hour smoke test at 25/50/100% traffic, rollback window of 2 hours.

Attachments: I’m attaching our draft capacity estimates and the commit matrix template so your team can fill in any missing traffic assumptions.

Action items for you: share the 48-hour traffic sample and confirm whether tokenization might increase average token lengths (we saw longer tokenization for clinical notes previously).

- Karthik

Attachments: clearline_qps_estimates.xlsx (stub), redwood_commit_matrix.pdf (stub)

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com, Anna Lopez <anna@clearlinehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity handover & cutover sequencing — Clearline Health

Looping in a couple of practical sizing notes from infra:

- For the 1.2x staging pool Karthik mentioned, we recommend reserving 8 x A100-80GB (or equivalent quantized nodes) for the US-EAST primary and 2 x A100-80GB for the hot DR. That maps to our latency goals with the expected prompt mix.
- We’ll enable prefix KV caching for common preambles and set batching windows at 8–12ms to keep p50 tight.
- Preflight checklist for SRE: model variant pins (v1.4-quant), warm KV caches, and a backend roll-forward path if we see >1% degradation during smoke.

Mina — can you prepare an ops runbook snippet (smoke commands, metrics thresholds, rollback steps) for the Jan window? I’ll coordinate resource reservations with the capacity team after Anna confirms the traffic sample.

—Ben

From: Anna Lopez <anna@clearlinehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@clearlinehealth.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2026 09:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity handover & cutover sequencing — Clearline Health

Karthik, Ben —

Thanks, that plan is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- Confirmed traffic sample attached (see separate secure upload). Peak numbers are validated with our load balancer team.
- Tokenization: clinical notes will run ~1.8x token inflation vs plain text; we’ll include a 1.8 multiplier in the XLS you sent.
- Procurement: we need an A/R milestone (post-cutover acceptance) tied to the DocuSign order. Procurement will only sign off after the 2-hour acceptance smoke that meets the SLA.

Procurement note included: please route the final acceptance checklist via DocuSign so we can sign within 48 hours of acceptance.

On a process note: could we include a secondary rollback strategy that shifts traffic back to Hosted API while keeping Dedicated warm for 24 hours? That will reduce risk on our end.

Anna

Anna / Procurement —

Appreciate the prompt confirmations. Based on the tokenization multiplier and the traffic sample you uploaded, here’s the updated plan and timeline (please review and ack):

- Nov 23–27: Redwood preflight run (staging mirror at 150 rps nominal). Deliverable: preflight report with p50/p95 metrics and memory/KV hit rates.
- Nov 30–Dec 3: Performance tuning sprint (kernel tweaks, batch window tuning, quantization profile lock). Deliverable: tuned model image and stability report.
- Dec 6–10: Ops runbook & commit matrix finalization. Redwood will generate the DocuSign-ready acceptance checklist.
- Jan 6 (proposed): Cutover day — 4-hour window starting 02:00–06:00 UTC. Sequence: 0–60m DNS cut/fanout to Dedicated at 25% traffic; 60–120m ramp to 50%; 120–180m ramp to 100% + 1-hour full-load smoke.

Rollback strategy: if p95 > 250ms or >0.5% error rate at any stage, we will route traffic back to Hosted API, keep Dedicated warm for 24 hours, and run a post-mortem.

Acceptance milestone: once the 1-hour full-load smoke meets SLA, Redwood will send the acceptance PDF for DocuSign within 4 hours. Procurement can sign within 48 hours to trigger the committed reserved capacity billing.

Operational notes:
- Infra resources to reserve now: 8 x A100-80GB (US-EAST), 2 x A100-80GB (US-WEST DR).
- Jira ticket for cutover runbook: RED-OPS-1423
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/CLH-7890

Please reply with a single-line ACK from procurement and Anna so we can lock reservations.

Thanks — Karthik
